Body:
**TL;DR**: Qwen3.7 Plus via OpenCode Go times out after 120s because Cloudflare in front of `opencode.ai` kills the connection with a 524 error. The server returns a Cloudflare HTML
 page, which the AI SDK can't parse as JSON — so the error message falls back to an empty status text, producing the cryptic `AI_APICallError: <none>`. The root cause is a missing
 server-side translation of 524 responses into parseable JSON errors.

---

I've been debugging this same issue in depth on the client side and wanted to share
the technical root cause I found — the `AI_APICallError: <none>` message hides what's
actually happening under the hood.

## Root Cause

The Qwen API response takes longer than 120 seconds end-to-end, and Cloudflare in
front of `opencode.ai` kills the connection with a **524 timeout**. The client SDK
never receives a proper JSON error, so it falls back to an empty status text and
produces the cryptic `AI_APICallError: <none>`.

Here's the exact request chain (captured via debug logging on the client):

 ```

 Client (@ai-sdk/anthropic)
   → POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages       ← Anthropic SDK appends /messages
     → Cloudflare (protecting opencode.ai)               ← 120s proxy read timeout
       → Zen origin (OpenCode Go backend)
         → upstream: dashscope-us.aliyuncs.com (Qwen API)
           → [generation takes >120 seconds]
         ← origin still waiting
       ← Cloudflare 120s timeout fires
     ← 524 HTML error page: "opencode.ai | 524: A timeout occurred"

 ```

## Why the error message is `<none>`

The Cloudflare 524 response comes back as **HTML** (not JSON), so the
`@ai-sdk/anthropic` SDK's `createJsonErrorResponseHandler` can't parse it.
It falls back to `response.statusText` as the error message — but for HTTP
status 524 the status text is empty, producing `APICallError({ message: "" })`.

## Why retries happen

`APICallError` with status 524 sets `isRetryable: true`, so the AI SDK
automatically retries. Eventually retry limits exhaust and the error surfaces
to the user as `"stream error" AI_APICallError: <none>`.

## Response headers (captured from the actual 524)

 ```

 server: cloudflare
 cf-ray: a104f190189e208d-IAD
 content-type: text/html; charset=UTF-8

 ```

Response body starts with `<!DOCTYPE html>` — confirming HTML, not JSON.

## Note on the endpoint URL

The actual URL used is `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages` — the `/go`
segment comes from the model falling back to the provider-level API base
(`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` from the models.dev catalog). This differs
from `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/messages` documented in the Zen docs.
The `/messages` suffix is added by `@ai-sdk/anthropic`.

## Suggested fix

The Zen API handler (`handler.ts:264`) currently only checks for status codes
`[400, 404, 429]` when deciding whether to return a proper JSON error response.
Adding 5xx codes — particularly 524 — to that list so the handler returns
`{"error": {"type": "timeout", "message": "..."}}` instead of passing through
the raw Cloudflare HTML would give the AI SDK a parseable error and show
users a meaningful message.

As a client-side fallback, `provider/error.ts`'s `message()` function could
also detect HTML error bodies with status 524 and produce a human-readable
string instead of `<none>`.
it's `ctrl+a` and `ctrl+e` in default bindings instead

Please have a look at this PR: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/33504
I am quite sure it will fix your problems too.

Also: could you please provide information which provider you are using.
There are too many graphics and moving part and sections, I like to have simpler option or ability to customize it myself, to something feels more like a terminal based tool.

@fwang I am quite sure this 524 error I got in my tests is something most likely the infrastructure team of Anomaly has to solve by itself. But I am willing to provide a PR to at least output a decent error message for that error type in the log.

> [@mekedron](https://github.com/mekedron) that's weird. It works for me...my setup: Mac, Ghostty, NeoVim (default editor), OpenCode, TMUX
> 
> Note: I'm not part of the dev team, just giving my two cents (and the tmux thing is probably irrelevant, but adds additional complexity that could possibly break this -- and it doesn't).
> 
> My understanding is it should work like this (and that's what I've observed in my setup):
> 
> * there's a TUI session (and a prompt)
> * when you select editor and open the prompt in the editor, it's exported as `<timestamp>.md` file and stored in a central location..something like `/private/var/folders/..../`.md` (on Mac)
> * you edit that file in the editor and when you save and exit (`:wq`) the TUI pulls the `.md` file and fills the prompt
> 
> So yeah...take this and debug or ask your favourite LLM for help

but if i save the words by `:wq`,then i has no chance to edit them again,right?this is a big problem for me,i think.
